title: Tormach post: the first XY traverse after a tool change rides at the top of Z even when that is below the part's clearance (Hub: down, over, up)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
**Found in a PathPilot Hub run (770MX sim, v2.14.4, 2026-11-13)** of the merged #1357 golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/drill_peck.nc`, posted inch for the 770MX.

**What happened.** In Hub's tool table T4 is 5.0000" long. With the session's G54 Z zero, the top of Z travel was only about 4.3" above work Z0. The program runs:

```
G53 G0 Z0        (top of travel)
G30
T4 M6
G43 H4           (5" tool: the tip is now about 0.68" BELOW work Z0, though nothing moved)
S1500 M3
M8
G0 X0.7874 Y0.3937       <- the XY traverse at that height: below the part top
G0 X0.7874 Y0.3937 Z0    <- then UP to Z0
```

The user saw the tool go down, then over, then up. "Down" is the 5" length offset taking effect. "Over" is the XY rapid with the tip about 0.68" below the stock surface. "Up" is the rapid to Z0. On a real machine that traverse would drive the tool through the part or the vise. At load time PathPilot warned "Program exceeds machine maximum on Z axis by 0.5107 in (line 0)", but the post still writes a traverse that cannot clear.

**Cause.** `tormach.cps` (`xyFirst` / `startXY`) makes the first XY move after a tool change "at the current - safe, Z-up - height". It assumes the top of travel is above the part. It never states the section's clearance Z before the traverse. When the tool is too long for the work offset, the top of travel is below that clearance.

**Proposed fix.** After `G43 H..`, and before the first XY traverse, write `G0 Z<clearance>` from the section's `ClearancePlane` (or its first rapid's Z). On a setup that can clear, this is an ordinary move down to clearance. On a setup that cannot, the control refuses the block as beyond its Z limit and stops. That is a visible refusal, not a rapid through the part. Pin it with a test: a stream whose first XY rapid follows a tool change shows `G0 Z<clearance>` before it. Regenerate the Tormach goldens this moves (listed in the PR). Check whether the other mill posts share the assumption, and file each one that does.

**Done means:** no Tormach program makes its first XY traverse after a tool change without first stating the clearance Z. That is pinned by a test, and the moved goldens are listed in the PR.

Related: #1357 (merged), the Hub session screenshots of 2026-11-13 17:55.
